NEW DELHI: India on Thursday rebuked Pakistan over its remarks on Kashmir and minorities in India at the UN Human Rights Council, calling out Islamabad for its illegal occupation of parts of Jammu and Kashmir and demanding that it vacate them.Exercising India's right to reply to the comments made by Pakistan at the council, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi advised Islamabad to direct its energy towards a debt-ridden economy surviving on bailouts rather than harbouring territorial ambitions or sponsoring cross-border terrorism."Since Pakistan appears to need the reminder under every agenda item, Jammu and Kashmir was, is and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India. The only part of Jammu and Kashmir under foreign occupation is the part Pakistan holds, which we again call upon it to vacate," Tyagi said."India is home to one of the largest Muslim populations in the world and our minorities vote, legislate, sit on a highest court and lead our institutions. In Pakistan, Hindu, Sikh and Christian communities have shrunk drastically since independence. Their daughters are abducted, forcibly converted and married off.Blasphemy laws hang over every minority household. Its own Muslim minorities, Shias, Ahmadiyyas, Ismailis and Hazaras face systemic persecution and their places of worship are attacked and desecrated," he added.Exposing this blatant double standard, Kshitij Tyagi said, "The Council does not need Pakistan to explain what happened in 1990 to the Kashmiri Pandits driven from their homes by terrorists Pakistan armed, trained and sent across the border.""Those same terrorists have since killed Kashmiris of every faith, many of them Muslim. The State that sponsored them is now asking this Council for an inquiry. The irony will not be lost on this Council," he added.Meanwhile, ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal issued a stern rejection of a letter circulated by Pakistan to the UN Security Council concerning a Court of Arbitration pronouncement on the Indus Waters Treaty, castigating Islamabad for twisting international legal mechanisms.Exposing Pakistan's systemic falsehoods, Randhir Jaiswal stated, "Regarding the 'permanent court' or so-called 'Permanent Court of Arbitration', I would like to say that Pakistan has a habit of misrepresenting facts and propagating falsehoods to serve its malicious propaganda."Reiterating India's principled and unyielding legal position, Randhir Jaiswal added, "For starters, the so-called ruling is not a ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration as sought to be projected by the Pakistan minister. It is a ruling by an illegally-constituted court. We see this as just another attempt by Pakistan at distorting reality. Our position on this issue is very clear and we have reiterated it several times. "
Article Summary: India rebukes Pakistan over its remarks on Kashmir and minorities in India at the UN Human Rights Council. India calls out Islamabad for its illegal occupation of parts of Jammu and Kashmir and demanding that it vacate them. India rejects letter circulated by Pakistan to UN Security Council concerning a Court of Arbitration pronouncement on Indus Waters Treaty.

Article Title: 2027 UP assembly polls: Fight against BJP or Congress? Why Akhilesh’s ‘rath’ show in Raebareli is message for Rahul
Article Text:
Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav during a visit to Raebareli. (PTI photo)

INDIA bloc's failed Bihar experiment

Rahul or Akhilesh vs BJP

The Owaisi factor

Lok Sabha gains, assembly pains

NEW DELHI: Is Uttar Pradesh all set to go the Bihar way for the opposition’s INDIA bloc? Wait, we are not talking about the results yet. This is about the all-too-familiar alliance strains between INDIA bloc allies - the Samajwadi Party and the Congress in the run-up to UP assembly elections early next year.On Thursday, Akhilesh Yadav unveiled the Samajwadi Party's 'PDA Rath' which he will use for a statewide campaign in the run-up to the 2027 assembly poll. While his fight is against the BJP, the first stop of his rath was Raebareli - a Congress bastion represented by the Gandhis for decades.Also, while Akhilesh targeted the BJP, he had a clear message for the Congress also.“Alliance will happen. We will also go with the alliance. Winnability will be the criteria for deciding seats. For us, it is not about seats, it is about victory. Whosoever can win can take the seat.”The BJP was quick to take digs at both allies and suggested that now Congress should start its campaign from Yadav bastion Mainpuri.This was not an isolated remark. The SP and the Congress have been engaged in a war of words over seat sharing for quite some time now. The open fight has an uncanny resemblance to how events had unfolded between the INDIA bloc allies in Bihar.Cut to the 2025 Bihar assembly elections.INDIA bloc allies - the RJD and the Congress engaged in a continuous war of words in Bihar over seat-sharing and CM face, while the BJP-led NDA managed a smooth division of seats. What started as public posturing between INDIA bloc allies ended up in public sparring between them as the divided opposition alliance was decimated in the polls.The two parties campaigned separately for most of the time as they could not agree on seat sharing. They took out separate yatras across the state. While Rahul Gandhi undertook the “Vote Adhikar Yatra,” RJD’s Tejashwi Yadav went across the state with his “Bihar Adhikar Yatra.” Ironically, it was the success of the two yatras that boomeranged on the alliance as it made seat-sharing bitter and difficult.In the run-up to the Bihar elections, Tejashwi Yadav was confident of a sweep. The Congress was also not willing to budge, guided by its improved showing in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in the state. The two parties used pressure tactics against each other. So much so that the INDIA bloc went into the elections as a divided house despite last-minute agreements and adjustments to keep the alliance intact.Uttar Pradesh appears to be headed the same way, at least as of now. We have already seen a lot of public posturing and sparring between the leaders of the INDIA bloc partners. Both the Congress and the SP have repeatedly claimed that the opposition’s fight against the BJP can be led only by their respective leaders.The SP and Congress contested the 2024 Lok Sabha polls together in Uttar Pradesh and won 43 seats between them, with the SP winning 37 and the Congress six. The alliance also won the Faizabad seat, which includes Ayodhya, where the BJP won in 2019.And that is perhaps where lies the genesis of this power tussle. Both the SP and the Congress feel that it was their party and leader who played a greater role in the 2024 electoral success and hence want the advantage to flow accordingly in seat sharing for the assembly elections.One look at the latest broadside between the two parties and we know why seat sharing between them may not be smooth.Recently, Samajwadi Party MP from Kairana Iqra Hasan and Congress MP from Saharanpur Imran Masood, both elected in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls as part of the SP-Congress alliance, publicly pitched their respective party leaders to take on the BJP."Only Rahul Gandhi is the opposition voice across the country, which unnerves the BJP. Rahul ji has done the hard work and created a favourable atmosphere. So make no mistake, nothing is possible without Rahul ji, and no one should have any doubts about this," Masood said.Days later, Hasan responded and pitched SP chief Yadav as the key to the alliance's prospects."Only Akhilesh Yadav is capable of defeating the BJP. On its own, the Congress won't be able to achieve much," she said.Last week, Congress Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam signalled a firm stance regarding upcoming electoral negotiations and said that any seat-sharing arrangement with the Samajwadi Party (SP) must be built on mutual respect and equal standing.Clarifying reports regarding seat distribution, Gautam claimed that formal discussions with the SP have not yet begun. While expressing open flexibility for minor adjustments, he stressed that the Congress would not compromise its organisational self-respect or dignity in any prospective deal."We have made one thing very clear. The Congress is the country's oldest party. It was the Congress that led the freedom struggle. Any alliance formed will be based on mutual respect; there will be equal partnership and dignity. Sure, we can show some flexibility; there might be minor adjustments, but we cannot compromise on our dignity," the Congress leader said.The contrasting assertions come despite messages of unity from both sides of the divide. Akhilesh is riding high on SP’s Lok Sabha success in Uttar Pradesh. The Congress, which is trying hard to revive its lost electoral fortunes, does not want to compromise on its expansion plans in one of the most politically important states.The problem is that both the parties are wooing the same social base in the state - minorities, Dalits, women, youth. Akhilesh is missing no opportunity to expand his PDA’s - Pichda Dalit and Alpsankhyak - base by making concerted attempts to include Pandits, Aadhi aabadi (women) and other social groups. The Congress is also wooing the Brahmins, the Dalits and the women in a big way.What the two bickering allies don't realise that there are several other parties who are also reaching out to the same social base. For instance, Mayawati and Chandrashekhar Azad are also going all out to woo Dalits. Then there is Owaisi, who has already put both the parties in a Catch22 situation by offering them an alliance against the BJP. Owaisi's proposal is like a double-edged sword for the two parties. If they accept his offer, the BJP will gun for them.If they reject the offer, Owaisi will use the rejection to rally the Muslims against them.The Samjawadi Party and the Congress may do well to learn lessons from the Bihar debacle before it’s too late. Lok Sabha elections and assembly elections are two very different games and success in one does not automatically translate into success in another. There are numerous instances to show that alliances which did well in Lok Sabha elections failed in assembly elections. Maharashtra is a case in point. The Maha Vikas Aghadi of the opposition parties - Congress, Shiv Sena and the NCP did very well in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, putting the BJP on the backfoot. But a year later in 2025 - the opposition alliance was decimated by the BJP in the assembly elections. So, Akhilesh and Rahul need to decide if they want to keep on flexing muscles at each other or unite in time to pose a challenge to the BJP.
Article Summary: The Samajwadi Party and the Congress have been engaged in a war of words over seat sharing for quite some time now. The open fight has an uncanny resemblance to how events had unfolded between the INDIA bloc allies in Bihar. The SP and Congress contested the 2024 Lok Sabha polls together in Uttar Pradesh and won 43 seats between them.

Article Title: When food becomes a philosophy
Article Text:
“Pon karaya kaayum, mann karaya peyyum”

Pathitrupathu

Pulal Maruththal

“Kollaan Pulalai Maruththaanai Kaikooppi

Ella Uyirum Thozhum.”

ahimsa

Chandogya Upanishad

Purataasi arrives with the fragrance of devotion. The sixth month of the Tamil calendar, dedicated to Lord Vishnu, is a month when many Tamil households voluntarily give up non-vegetarian food . Even confirmed meat lovers submit to this discipline. Some of my friends go berserk on the last day of Aavani, indulging in every imaginable meat delicacy!But Purataasi is more than a month of prayer. It is also a month of climatic transition. An old Tamil saying describes its extremes vividly:— the heat is so fierce that gold may melt, and the rain so heavy that the earth may erode. Perhaps, a gentler diet could give the digestive system some respite while the body adjusted to the changing weather.Vegetarianism itself must have emerged much later in the journey of humankind. Our earliest ancestors were certainly hunters and meat-eaters., in Sangam literature for instance, describes a preparation in which red meat was cooked with pulses and mixed with white rice — a dish that sounds remarkably like a distant ancestor of today's biryani.And yet, Thiruvalluvar gave vegetarianism an extraordinary ethical dimension. He devoted an entire chapter to— the refusal of meat. In Kural 260, he says:“One who does not kill and refuses to eat meat is worshipped by all living beings.”Valluvar did not present vegetarianism merely as a religious injunction. He seemed to locate it in something more elemental — compassion. His argument begins not with food, but with the refusal to cause harm.This has naturally led some scholars to see a possible Jain influence in Valluvar's thought. Jainism places, or non-violence, at the heart of spiritual life, and vegetarianism became one of its most rigorous expressions. The Jain understanding of food is deeply connected with the avoidance of harm and the accumulation of karma.The Jain tradition traces a powerful story of renunciation to Prince Neminatha, regarded as the 22nd Tirthankara. Neminatha was on his way to his wedding when he heard the cries of animals gathered to be slaughtered for the wedding feast. He turned away from the marriage, renounced his royal life and embraced the path of a Jain monk. The story transforms food into a moral question: what price should another life pay for our appetite?Interestingly, thespeaks of a teacher who instructed Krishna in asceticism and non-violence. Historian D D Kosambi suggested that this teacher may have been Neminatha himself, though this remains a historical conjecture.Today, vegetarianism has acquired another dimension. The growing popularity of veganism in the West is partly driven by concerns about animal welfare and the environmental footprint of livestock farming. Yet, paradoxically, in India — traditionally home to the world's largest vegetarian population — dietary habits are increasingly moving in the opposite direction.Perhaps the enduring wisdom of Valluvar lies not in telling us what must be on our plate, but in asking what lies within our heart. For him, refusing meat was not simply about food. It was about whether the mind could remain indifferent to the suffering of another living being.Sometimes, what we choose not to consume can reveal more about us than what we eat.
Article Summary: The sixth month of the Tamil calendar, dedicated to Lord Vishnu, is a month when many Tamil households voluntarily give up non-vegetarian food. The growing popularity of veganism in the West is partly driven by concerns about animal welfare. Yet, paradoxically, in India, dietary habits are increasingly moving in the opposite direction.

NEW DELHI: Over 220 sight-restoring surgeries were conducted by Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) surgeons during the 10th edition of first-of-its-kind mega eye surgical camp, held under Operation Drishti, at an underground operation theatre in a shelling-prone zone at Tangdhar in Kupwara along the Line of Control in J&K on Friday and Saturday.Most interventions were cataract surgeries, along with selective retinal procedures and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery. Patients from Khawarpora, Tangdar, Tadd, Bagbela, Yangdar and neighbouring hamlets came after screening and a broadcast on Radio Rooh-e-Karnah, with the Indian Army guiding each one from arrival to recovery.Over the two days, the camp was visited by Army chief General Dhiraj Seth who interacted with patients and distributed medicines and gifts. DG AFMS Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja also visited the camp and appreciated the surgeons and their team. The camp was led by head of ophthalmology at Army Hospital (Research & Referral), Delhi Cantonment Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra, whose team carried advanced phacoemulsification, vitreoretinal and glaucoma equipment across mountainous terrain.AFMS’s series of mega surgical eye camps envisaged by defence minister Rajnath Singh has, so far, screened over 1.5 lakh patients. Over 3,500 surgeries have been conducted across 10 cities. The 11th camp in this series will be held in Srinagar from Sept 27 to 29. The formal closing ceremony will be attended by J&K LG Manoj Sinha on Sept 30.
Article Summary: Most interventions were cataract surgeries, along with selective retinal procedures and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery. Patients from Khawarpora, Tangdar, Tadd, Bagbela, Yangdar and neighbouring hamlets came after screening and broadcast on Radio Rooh-e-Karnah.

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday welcomed the first ascent mountaineering expedition team, which successfully summited 20 previously unclimbed peaks above 6,000 meters in Ladakh in just 23 days.The flag-in ceremony was held at Kartavya Bhavan-2 in New Delhi, in the presence of the defence minister and other senior officials.According to the defence ministry, the expedition was carried out by a team of 20 highly skilled climbers from the National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports (NIMAS), Dirang, led by Col Ranveer Singh Jamwal.Speaking with the team, Rajnath praised the climbers' courage and determination in achieving this historic feat, calling the expedition a reflection of India's excellence and leadership in mountaineering and adventure sports.He described the climbers as a source of inspiration, noting that their successful ascents had set new benchmarks and would motivate young mountaineers across the country to take up adventure and exploration while bringing pride to the nation.The ministry applauded the expedition group's planning, technical skill, endurance and teamwork, and said it highlighted the country's high-altitude mountaineering capabilities and reinforced its standing on the global mountaineering map.This is the first-ever recorded summit of 20 unclimbed peaks in Chamser-Lungser, Gyama Nala, and ⁠Chokula areas in Ladakh Range," the ministry said.
Article Summary: First-ever recorded summits of 20 unclimbed peaks in Chamser-Lungser, Gyama Nala and ⁠Chokula areas in Ladakh Range. Expedition carried out by a team of 20 highly skilled climbers from the National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports.

Article Title: 'Becoming a good citizen more important': BJP chief Nitin Nabin's message to youth amid party's outreach push
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Friday urged young people to focus on becoming “good citizens”, saying it is "more important" than becoming a good engineer or doctor.“One may become a good engineer or doctor, but becoming a good citizen is more important,” PTI quoted Nabin as saying at a ‘Yuva Samvad’ programme at Birla Auditorium in Jaipur.He further advised youngsters not to fear failure and to avoid shortcuts in life, saying this would lead them to the right destination.“Life is precious. If you face failure, you should not immediately go in the wrong direction or put your life at stake. If we have been given this life, we should do something meaningful for our parents and for this land,” the BJP chief added.Nabin also called for greater youth participation in politics, saying it gives “direction to the country” and that leadership is not merely about making policies but also about bringing people together.During the interaction, several young participants shared their views and suggestions on issues including the constructive use of artificial intelligence, keeping young people away from drugs, and the role of youth clubs in schools and colleges in building a developed India by 2047.Nabin’s remarks come at a time when political parties are reaching out extensively to young people, particularly the “Gen Z” demographic, following youth protests that led to the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July. Pradhan resigned amid the controversy over the NEET paper leak in May and other issues concerning the education sector.Gen Z is expected to make up a significant section of India’s young population by the time the country holds its next Lok Sabha elections in 2029.
Article Summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin urges young people to focus on becoming "good citizens" He also called for greater youth participation in politics. Nabin’s remarks come at a time when political parties are reaching out to young people, particularly the ‘Gen Z’ demographic.

NEW DELHI: Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor on Friday said the “rot” in the Election Commission of India (ECI) began well before Gyanesh Kumar became Chief Election Commissioner (CEC). His remarks came amid a massive row following a media report alleging differences between Kumar and the two Election Commissioners over several decisions, including the contentious Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.“The rot did not begin with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The EC, by its partiality, has been ensuring that those in a close fight with the BJP ended up tasting defeat and those tipped for a massive victory won only by a modest margin," he said.Kishor had worked with the Trinamool Congress during the 2021 West Bengal assembly elections and played a key role in the party securing a third consecutive term.He also cited his experience in the recent bypoll to Bihar’s Bankipur Assembly seat, which he won in his electoral debut.“I would have won by at least 50,000 votes, but for the EC turning a blind eye to the blatant misuse of the administrative machinery and the BJP’s spending of hundreds of crores during the campaign,” Kishor alleged. He wrested the seat from the BJP, which had held it for 30 years. The seat had fallen vacant after BJP national president Nitin Nabin's resignation as MLA following his election as a Rajya Sabha MP.The JSP founder also claimed that the “conduct of elections is compromised on all counts”, including campaign funding, the use of the bureaucracy and alleged tampering with electoral rolls.

Article Title: The Backstory: When 'Tau' Devi Lal won the PM race, and then gave it away with a twist
Article Text:
Chaudhary Devi Lal, the former Haryana chief minister and deputy prime minister, who turned down the Prime Minister's post in 1989 in favour of VP Singh.

The Central Hall manoeuvre

The OG 'Tau'

From Haryana's farmer leader to national kingmaker

The shifting dynamics

Legacy that became a political dynasty

NEW DELHI: On December 1, 1989, the newly elected Janata Dal parliamentary party gathered in Parliament's Central Hall to decide who would lead the government that was about to replace Rajiv Gandhi's Congress. The leadership contest had already become a tug-of-war between VP Singh and Chandra Shekhar, with neither side willing to concede the top job.Then came an extraordinary political manoeuvre.VP Singh proposed Chaudhary Devi Lal's name. Chandra Shekhar seconded it. Devi Lal was declared elected as leader of the Janata Dal parliamentary party. And then the 75-year-old Haryana veteran stood up and proposed VP Singh for the Prime Minister post.Within minutes, the man who had just been chosen to lead the government had handed the job to someone else.VP Singh was elected leader and would become India's seventh Prime Minister. Devi Lal became deputy Prime Minister.The episode, one of the more remarkable leadership reversals in political history, has been recounted in several accounts of the 1989 transition. But this story is about Chaudhary Devi Lal, a man whose influence was built far from Delhi's power corridors and whose appeal rested heavily on Haryana's farmers and rural voters.The drama of December 1 was the culmination of days of uncertainty following the 1989 Lok Sabha election, which had ended Rajiv Gandhi's five-year tenure and produced a fractured mandate.The National Front, led by the Janata Dal, was in a position to form the government with outside support from the BJP and the Left parties. But before the government could be formed, the Janata Dal had to settle its own leadership question.VP Singh was the obvious national face of the anti-Congress campaign, having broken with Rajiv Gandhi and built his reputation around allegations of corruption in the previous government. Chandra Shekhar, meanwhile, had his own ambitions and was deeply reluctant to accept Singh as the party's leader.Devi Lal sat at the centre of the equation.A detailed account of the episode in journalist Neerja Chowdhury's 'How Prime Ministers Decide' describes a political formula worked out at Odisha Bhavan shortly before the parliamentary party meeting. The plan was simple but dramatic: Singh would propose Devi Lal's name, Devi Lal would then withdraw and propose Singh, and Chandra Shekhar would be persuaded to second Devi Lal's nomination.Chandra Shekhar agreed to second Devi Lal's name after being told that Devi Lal would be the candidate. He did not, however, know the full plan.When the meeting began in Central Hall, the arrangement played out almost exactly as planned. Singh proposed Devi Lal. Chandra Shekhar seconded him. But after Devi Lal's nomination, the Haryana leader proposed Singh instead. The assembled parliamentarians broke into applause and Singh was declared leader of the Janata Dal Parliamentary Party.Chandra Shekhar was furious.According to the account, he believed he had been assured that Devi Lal would become Prime Minister. After the meeting, he reportedly warned that the episode would have consequences for the future.That warning proved prescient. Less than a year later, Chandra Shekhar and Devi Lal would join forces against VP Singh, helping bring down the government they had helped create.Born on September 25, 1914, in what was then Punjab, Devi Lal entered politics through the freedom movement and went on to become one of Haryana's most influential leaders.He served as Haryana chief minister twice, from 1977 to 1979 and again from 1987 to 1989, before becoming deputy Prime Minister at the Centre.His political persona was very different from that of the Delhi establishment. Devi Lal cultivated the image of a rustic, accessible farmer leader and became popularly known as 'Tau', or elder uncle.Former IAS officer Ram Varma, who spent more than three decades in Haryana's administration and worked under all three of the state's famous political Lals, provides an insider's account of Devi Lal in his 2017 memoir 'Life in the IAS: My Encounters with the Three Lals of Haryana'.Varma describes Devi Lal as having the "aura of a kingmaker" and as a "leader of farmers", while portraying him as a warm and genial personality with an exceptionally strong mass following.Varma's description also places Devi Lal in the distinctive political tradition of Haryana's three Lals. In the book's foreword, he notes that Bansi Lal was the only one of the three to possess a university degree, while Devi Lal and Bhajan Lal acquired their political education through the "rough and tumble" of village-level politics. He records that Devi Lal had earlier served as parliamentary secretary under Punjab CM Partap Singh Kairon, giving him administrative experience before Haryana was created in 1966.That combination of grassroots politics and governmental experience helped turn Devi Lal into a formidable political operator.Devi Lal's influence had grown sharply by the late 1980s, when opposition parties were attempting to unite against Rajiv Gandhi's Congress.He became one of the principal forces behind the formation of the Janata Dal and helped bring disparate opposition groups into a common political platform. His enormous rural base in Haryana gave the anti-Congress coalition an organisational strength that leaders in Delhi could not easily ignore.His political stature was also on display in September 1989, when his 75th birthday became the occasion for a massive opposition rally in Delhi. VP Singh and several other opposition leaders attended, underlining the importance of Devi Lal in the emerging National Front coalition.Yet the relationship between the two men was more complicated than their public alliance suggested.VP Singh was the face of the anti-Rajiv Gandhi campaign at the national level, while Devi Lal possessed something Singh lacked: a formidable rural organisation and an established mass base in north India.By the time the election results were out, the question was no longer simply whether the opposition could form a government. It was who would control it.At around 7 pm on December 1, 1989, VP Singh met President R Venkataraman at Rashtrapati Bhavan with the documents establishing his election as leader of the National Front parliamentary party, along with letters of support from the BJP and Left parties. Venkataraman invited Singh to form the government and set December 2 for the swearing-in.The following day, VP Singh took oath as Prime Minister and Devi Lal took oath as deputy Prime Minister.But the political bargain did not bring lasting peace.The relationship between Singh and Devi Lal deteriorated rapidly as their competing political interests collided. Devi Lal became increasingly critical of the Prime Minister and emerged as the most powerful internal challenger to Singh.In August 1990, Singh removed Devi Lal from the Union cabinet. The following months saw the Janata Dal split, the BJP withdraw support and the VP Singh government fall.On November 9, 1990, Chandra Shekhar became Prime Minister with Devi Lal once again serving as deputy Prime Minister.Devi Lal's influence did not end with his death. It flowed into one of Haryana's most prominent political families.His son Om Parkash Chautala became one of Haryana's most consequential politicians and served as CM five times. Devi Lal's political legacy was subsequently carried through the Indian National Lok Dal, the party associated with the Chautala family.The next generation entered politics as well. Om Parkash Chautala's sons Ajay and Abhay Chautala became prominent leaders, while Ajay's sons Dushyant and Digvijay Chautala also entered electoral politics.But the family eventually split politically. Ajay Chautala and Dushyant Chautala broke away and formed the Jannayak Janta Party in 2018, while the INLD remained with Om Parkash Chautala and Abhay Chautala.The split fractured what had once been a formidable political inheritance. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, neither the INLD nor the JJP won a seat in Haryana, while the BJP and Congress won five seats each in the state.The contrast with Devi Lal's own era is striking. The man whose political clout once helped determine who would become India's Prime Minister left behind a family whose branches now operate through separate political formations.Devi Lal died in New Delhi on April 6, 2001, aged 86, after a political career that had taken him from the freedom movement and Haryana's villages to the centre of national coalition politics.
Article Summary: Chaudhary Devi Lal was the former Haryana chief minister and deputy prime minister. He turned down the Prime Minister's post in 1989 in favour of VP Singh. The episode was one of the more remarkable leadership reversals in political history. Devi Lal cultivated the image of a rustic farmer and became popularly known as 'Tau'

Article Title: EC faultlines have a long history, dating back to 1989
Article Text:
Election Commission of India

Poll Vote & Share your view Which internal conflict within the Election Commission do you find most concerning? Seshan vs. Gill and Krishnamurthy Gopalaswami vs. Chawla Arora vs. Lavasa Goyal's resignation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: It is not the first time that the fault lines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989.Two election commissioners S S Dhanoa and V S Seigell were appointed in October 1989 and joined the poll body then led by chief election commissioner (CEC) R V S Peri Sastri. Though Sastri never publicly spoke about it, it is widely believed that the new arrangement was perceived by him as a dilution in power. By January 1990, the appointment of the two commissioners was rescinded and the EC reverted to being a single—member body.In 1993, with T N Seshan as an all-powerful CEC, the commission was once again made a multi-member body with the appointment of election commissioners M S Gill and G V G Krishnamurthy. What followed was a running feud between Seshan on the one hand and Gill and Krishnamurthy on the other. Seshan viewed the appointments as a direct assault on the independence of his office and completely refused to recognize the two new commissioners. He refused to share official documents with Gill and Krishnamurthy, barred them from attending critical meetings, and would not allocate them any office work. He openly ridiculed the election commissioners in interviews, even referring to them as “two donkeys in my office”.Interestingly, it was on Seshan’s plea challenging the govt’s decision to make EC a multi-member body that the Supreme Court had, in 1995, ruled that the election commissioners and CEC were equal in status, power and decision-making authority and that the CEC was only “first among equals”.The other internal feud in EC to recall would be one between then CEC N Gopalaswami and election commissioner Navin Chawla between 2006 and 2009. Months before he was to step down upon the end of his tenure, Gopalaswami wrote to the President of India recommending the removal of Chawla on grounds of a pro-Congress bias. In his note to the President, Gopalaswami alleged that Chawla was passing on details of EC’s meetings to senior Congress leaders, often taking “toilet breaks” during commission meetings to do so. Gopalaswami’s recommendation was however turned down by the Manmohan Singh govt and Chawla succeeded him as CEC.During the 2019 general election, the differences between then CEC Sunil Arora and then election commissioner Ashok Lavasa came to the fore, with media reports alleging that he had dissented in cases relating to complaints of alleged model code of conduct violations by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and then BJP president Amit Shah, but was overruled without the commission making his dissent noted public. EC put out a clarification that dissent notes were only made public in quasi-judicial orders passed by EC.Lavasa resigned on August 18, 2020, two years short of his tenure, and joined the Manila-headquartered Asian Development Bank (ADB) as its Vice-President.Arun Goyal was the last election commissioner to quit in the middle of his term. Though he had cited personal reasons in his resignation dated March 9, 2024, it was widely speculated that he was not on the best of terms with the then chief election commissioner Rajiv Kumar.
Article Summary: The fault lines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989. Two election commissioners S S Dhanoa and V S Seigell were appointed in October 1989 and joined the poll body then led by chief election commissioner R V S Peri Sastri.

Article Title: Kalkaji gang-rape: Police probe if Aastha Kunj park was hunting ground of accused
Article Text:

Call detail records, CCTV footage place three accused near park at time of crime





NEW DELHI: Police investigating the alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj park in south Delhi on Monday evening are trying to establish if the three accused have been involved in similar incidents earlier that have gone unreported.They were clearly looking for a vulnerable target, say police sources, with Asif - armed with a pistol and a condom in pocket - taking the lead in entering the park, followed by the two brothers, Hemant Singh and Mukesh Singh. They then teamed up to unleash 40 minutes of terror on the hapless couple.Police sources said the girl and her friend were sitting on a bench around 7:15 pm when the three men allegedly approached them, posing as policemen in civvies.Having intimidated the two teenagers, they took the boy around 200m away and slapped and threatened him before taking the girl to a secluded, dark stretch of the park. That's where they took turns to allegedly rape her. The girl was threatened against disclosing the incident to anyone.She was asked to leave the place immediately. By around 8pm, the men had left the spot, police said.According to the investigators, Hemant and Mukesh went out for dinner after that and returned home later. Asif seemed to be more cautious. Police got an early lead but couldn't find him either at the Okhla mandi or his house on Monday night.The girl returned to her friend and told him what had happened. The two left the park around 8:45pm. That's when the boy made a PCR call, which brought the cops to the park. The cops are now trying to establish how Asif had procured the pistol.They claim to have found "objectionable material", including videos, on Asif's phone, sources said. Some data was allegedly deleted from the phones of Hemant and Mukesh. These have been sent to Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for retrieval.So far, the police have not come across any old complaints against the three. "We are checking whether someone may not have filed a complaint because of threats," a senior police officer said.The police are pursuing this angle because the three men would often hang around the park in the late hours. Hemant and Mukesh have allegedly changed their statements frequently during questioning. At one point, they claimed they were at home when the incident took place but gave a different account later. Their call detail records and CCTV footage, however, allegedly placed them near the park at the time.Sources said police are also investigating allegations that Hemant was removed from a gym he frequented following complaints of misbehaviour against him. The three have been sent to judicial custody for two days.DDA is facing a lot of flak for not having improved security in the park despite being alerted at least three times by the police since 2025. The police have pointed out that there were no CCTV cameras inside the park.Sources in DDA said their horticulture department had written multiple letters in the past one year to increase patrolling at the park. "Nine security guards are deployed in each shift at strategic locations, along with supervisory and patrolling arrangements. The lighting installations in the Aastha Kunj Park are functional and are inspected regularly. However, installing cameras at each spot won't be practical," a DDA official said.Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar, meanwhile, visited Aastha Kunj Park around 8.15pm Tuesday. He patrolled the park with other officers and reviewed security arrangements in and around the premises. He also directed the officers to further strengthen security through increased motorcycle and foot patrols .
Article Summary: Police trying to establish if the three accused have been involved in similar incidents earlier that have gone unreported. Asif - armed with a pistol and a condom in pocket - took the lead in entering the park. Hemant and Mukesh Singh then teamed up to unleash 40 minutes of terror on the couple.

Article Title: In 2022, Miami Dolphins star Zach Sieler and his wife launched an outdoor foundation; four years later, their 250-acre Missouri property is becoming a farm and conservation classroom for children
Article Text:
Zach and Hannah’s foundation grew from a 2019 experience at their hunting camp with a wheelchair user.

Building outdoor lessons

Plans for farming and conservation

Reaching more children

Miami Dolphins defensive tackle and team captain Zach Sieler and his wife Hannah are developing their 250-acre property in Missouri into a place where children can learn about agriculture, conservation and the outdoors. The couple launched the Sieler Safe Haven Foundation as a non-profit in 2022, after an experience at their hunting camp led them to create more opportunities for young people to experience nature.Sieler spoke about the plans during his appearance on the Like A Farmer podcast, where he discussed football, fatherhood, farming, hunting and his family’s life outdoors. The episode also covers his plans to begin raising cattle on the Missouri property.The property is now part of the foundation’s work with children. The Sieler Safe Haven Foundation describes its Missouri site as a “hands-on learning laboratory where agriculture meets adventure”. Its programmes include experiences related to farming, wildlife, land management, fishing and hunting.The foundation’s work grew from an experience in 2019, when Zach and Hannah welcomed a young man who uses a wheelchair to their hunting camp.They realised that traditional hunting was not accessible to him and began thinking about how outdoor experiences could be made available to more young people. Three years later, they officially registered the foundation as a non-profit.The Sielers say their own experiences outdoors shaped their interest in creating such opportunities for children. Zach grew up in Pinckney, Michigan, where his father introduced him to hunting, fishing and outdoor activities on their 30-acre property.Hannah Sieler, who is from Ozark, Missouri, also had an active childhood, although she had limited experience camping in tents with her family. According to the foundation, her understanding of what young people can miss without exposure to the outdoors has influenced her work with the organisation.The foundation now runs programmes that combine outdoor education with activities such as agriculture, wildlife management, fishing, hunting and sports. It says these experiences are intended to help young people develop practical skills, confidence and an understanding of environmental stewardship.The foundation says participants can take part in turkey and whitetail deer hunts, fishing and activities involving wildlife and land management. The property also works with the Land Legacy Partnership on a plan for managing wildlife on the property.Sieler told Like A Farmer that his family plans to begin raising cattle in Missouri. The foundation also says land management is also part of its work in Missouri. Its partnership with the Land Legacy Partnership includes practices such as controlled burns, timber improvements and natural farming methods.The aim is not only to provide outdoor activities but also to teach young people about the land and how it is managed. The foundation describes these experiences as opportunities to understand land stewardship and sustainable living practices.The Missouri property is one part of the Sieler Safe Haven Foundation’s work. The organisation also runs programmes in Florida and Michigan and helps facilitate educational trips in other locations.In Florida, its programmes focus on fishing, wetland conservation, wildlife management and cultural enrichment. In Michigan, it offers programmes involving forest management, wildlife conservation and outdoor recreation.The foundation also organises other activities for children. These include sports camps, field days and outdoor experiences designed around conservation, agriculture and wildlife management.
Article Summary: Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler and his wife Hannah are developing their 250-acre property in Missouri into a place where children can learn about agriculture, conservation and the outdoors. The couple launched the Sieler Safe Haven Foundation as a non-profit in 2022. Its work grew from an experience in 2019, when Zach and Hannah welcomed a young man who uses a wheelchair to their hunting camp.

Article Title: In 1990, a car accident nearly killed Brett Favre before he ever threw an NFL pass; 3 decades later, the game is still sorting out how to remember a man who gave it everything and broke its heart
Article Text:
Brett Favre survived a near-fatal car accident at 20 and went on to build one of the most celebrated careers in NFL history (Getty Images)

What happened to Brett Favre in the 1990 car accident?

How is the NFL remembering Brett Favre now, more than a decade after his retirement?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brett Favre was 20 years old when a car crash on a rural Mississippi road left him with a 30-inch scar, a removed portion of his small intestine, and the kind of near-death moment that resets a person. He survived. He went on to throw 508 NFL touchdowns. He won a Super Bowl. He played through pain that would have sidelined most mortals. And then, in the years that followed his retirement, he made choices that have left the league genuinely unsure what to do with him.The summer of 1990 was not supposed to be the summer Brett Favre almost died. He was a 20-year-old college quarterback at Southern Miss, heading home. The car left the road, rolled, and when everything stopped moving, Favre was airlifted to a hospital in critical condition. Doctors removed 30 inches of his small intestine. He lost 34 pounds. And two months later, he was back on a football field.That story became foundational to the Favre mythology. Toughness. Resilience. A guy you just could not keep down. He played 297 consecutive regular-season games. He won three straight MVP awards. He dragged the Green Bay Packers to a Super Bowl title in 1996 and turned a franchise city into a religious experience for an entire generation of fans.There was something almost ridiculous about his durability, the way he played through a broken thumb, a sprained ankle, a torn ligament, sometimes all in the same season.But the mythology always sat on a more complicated foundation. The addiction to painkillers was real. His retirement-and-unretirement cycle wore out multiple front offices and created genuine damage in Minnesota, where his late-career run with the Vikings strained relationships that had been decades in the making. And then, long after the jersey was hung up, came the welfare fund scandal in Mississippi. Favre was accused of directing millions in state welfare funds toward projects that personally benefited him, including a volleyball facility at the university where his daughter played. He has denied knowingly doing anything wrong. The legal proceedings are ongoing.The NFL, for its part, has mostly stayed quiet. His bust is in Canton. His number is retired in Green Bay. But the league that once celebrated him on every highlight reel has grown noticeably quieter about the Favre brand in recent years.There is no clean answer, which is part of what makes this so uncomfortable for everyone involved. The Hall of Fame does not have a mechanism for revisionism. His records stand. The memories of those Monday night performances, those frozen-field moments, those throws that no rational quarterback should have attempted, those are not going anywhere.What has shifted is the tone. The NFL networks do not loop Favre content the way they once did. His appearances at league events have thinned. And within Green Bay, a city that made him a near-deity, there is a genuine and sometimes painful conversation happening about legacy versus accountability.Brett Favre himself has spoken about his health in recent years, revealing that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He has also become more vocal about the dangers of head trauma in football, a subject he admits he did not think much about while he was playing through every hit. That part of his story carries a different kind of weight now.What remains is a player who was, for a stretch of years in the 1990s, the most compelling figure in American sport. The guy who survived a crash at 20 and then played football like he had something to prove every single Sunday. The NFL has not figured out how to square that with what came after. It may not figure it out for a long time.
Article Summary: Brett Favre survived a near-fatal car accident at 20 and went on to build one of the most celebrated careers in NFL history. The league that once celebrated him on every highlight reel has grown noticeably quieter about the Favre brand in recent years.

For me, this is an Olympic medal. It’s no less than an Olympic medal. All the strongest teams come in the Asian contingent. So this feels like an Olympic medal to me because Soft Tennis is not part of the Olympics Jay Meena

Bigger than an Asian Games medal

NEW DELHI: Weeks before the 2026 Asian Games , Jay Meena was bedridden with typhoid and a severe infection, losing eight kilograms in the process. Sent home to Dewas in Madhya Pradesh from an Asian Games training camp in Srinagar in August, the 25-year-old needed his parents to feed him by hand for nearly a week.Recovery was difficult too. For a week, he would feel dizzy after walking just a few steps. An iffy stomach only made his attempts to regain his strength and return to shape more challenging.Cut to the present. The moment his opponent’s final shot drifted long and Meena won India’s first-ever Asian Games medal in Soft Tennis, the 25-year-old collapsed onto the baseline in joy. Moments later, he was back on his feet, arms spread wide and roaring towards the Indian bench. The celebration marked far more than a bronze medal. It was a historic moment for Indian Soft Tennis, with Meena securing the country’s first-ever Asian Games medal in the sport.Meena narrates that for 15 days, he was completely out of action and the clock on the Asian Games was ticking down. All his efforts over the course of the past few months had just been undone by the viral infection. “I started light warm-ups, I started training again.I could not sit at home at such a moment,” he tells TimesofIndia.com, with the urgency of the situation still quite evident in his voice.He recovered just in time to board the flight to Tokyo and the Shinkansen (train) to Nagoya. The ordeal, however, was far from over.Recovering from typhoid meant nutrition became almost as important as training. But in Nagoya, the predominantly seafood menu offered few vegetarian options. In the absence of a traditional Games village, he made do with corn, bread, butter, milk and cereal. While urging the authorities to send a chef alongside future contingents, Meena stressed that pre-packaged foods cannot replace fresh preparations.The lingering effects of the illness surfaced during his semi-final loss to Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka (2-4), as Meena required a medical timeout to continue the closely contested match at the Higashiyama Park Tennis Center.He later revealed that a hip niggle was preventing him from playing his backhand, with a “pinching” pain each time he went for the shot.Then there is the obvious mental challenge of representing the country at such a competition. Little by little, the chances of winning a medal got smaller and the internal battles got bigger. First, the men’s team, also featuring Meena, lost 0-2 to Indonesia in the quarter-finals. Then, Meena and Aadhya Tiwari lost in the first round of mixed doubles.“There were a lot of disappointing nights, a lot of self-doubts that we had all night. When we lost the quarter-final against Indonesia, it was a big opportunity on the 18th. If we had won that day, then Soft Tennis would have opened the (medal) account for India. After that, there was (the) mixed doubles in which Aadhya and I reached the pre-quarter-finals but lost. So, there were very disappointing nights going on day by day,” said Meena in reflection of the start of the competition.“After all these things, it was very difficult to come back and gain confidence after the self-doubt. It was very difficult to wake up every morning with new hope and get on the court with a new zeal,” he continued.A career that almost wasn't and brother's sacrificeThe desperate need for belief and confidence is not new to Meena’s career. When he was in Class 10 and his foray into Soft Tennis was not going anywhere, Rameshwar, his lawyer father, suggested stepping away and focusing elsewhere. It was then that his mother stepped in and pushed for a rethink and patience. That punt paid off.Years later, Meena began rewriting Indian Soft Tennis history, winning National Games gold, India’s first World Championships medal in mixed doubles, and a breakthrough Asian Championships bronze.Still one of his biggest supporters, Meena’s father travelled with his son to national tournaments and even accompanied him to Japan for the Asian Games.The hardest sacrifice, perhaps, belongs to someone else: his younger brother Yash.Two years younger than Jay, Yash was a Soft Tennis player and national medallist. But with their financial condition less than ideal, a hard decision was needed and Jay’s career continued.“The financial condition was not so good. We had to force him to stay back because my father could not afford more than what was costing me to play. That’s why he went into Engineering,” says the MP native.“Somewhere or the other, my younger brother’s life was sacrificed because of me. Because my parents paid more attention to me for about 10 years. If we had continued, then maybe he would have been with me in the Asian Games,” he continued.Jay Meena was like many other youngsters in the country who harboured cricket ambitions. He would play gully cricket with other kids in his street. The notorious boy in him, though, tended to pick up fights and get into altercations. Even at school, he would bother the teachers, including once setting off fireworks under his principal’s desk.The situation came to a head when he was rusticated from Ebenazer Higher Secondary School in the fourth grade. With no school willing to take him in, Pioneer Public School agreed, but on one condition: that he join the sports academy. With his parents keen on keeping Jay’s antics in check, they agreed to sports coach Sudesh Sangte’s condition.Sangte, a former national-level Kho Kho player and now the national Soft Tennis coach, had set up a two-court facility.“My family was very upset with me. I would not stay at home, I would not allow anyone to relax. I used to fight. Their parents used to complain a lot and my family threw me out. They said, you are out now. You stay on the ground [academy]. Don’t come home in the morning and evening. Come home at night,” Jay says with a laugh.“The school teachers and my classmates were (also) upset. I was rusticated in the fourth grade. And no other school was admitting me. At that time, Mr. Sudesh Sangte, who is my head coach now, he got me admitted. I took admission during the summer holidays.”“They had made two courts in their school. So, I was playing in their academy during the summer holidays. I didn’t even know, when I started playing for India and now won the Asian Games medal,” he explained.Even though the International Soft Tennis Federation (ISTF) has 65 members, including Eritrea, Basque Country, Curacao, Malta, North Korea and Uganda, the sport is dominated by Asian countries. At the last World Soft Tennis Championships, held in Anseong, South Korea, in 2024, six countries had picked up medals: Korea, Japan, Chinese Taipei, China, India and the Philippines.At the 2026 Asian Games, there were entries from 13 National Olympic Committees (NOCs), with Cambodia, Japan, South Korea, Mongolia, the Philippines and North Korea sending the maximum permissible 10 players. In the end, athletes from Japan, Chinese Taipei, North Korea, South Korea, Indonesia, India and the Philippines walked away with medals.Considering the dominance of Asian countries in Soft Tennis, Jay weighs this new medal on an Olympic scale.“For me, this is an Olympic medal. It’s no less than an Olympic medal. All the strongest teams come in the Asian contingent. So this feels like an Olympic medal to me because Soft Tennis is not part of the Olympics,” the youngster explained.Sixteen years ago, Soft Tennis was simply a way to keep an unruly fourth-grader out of trouble. Today, it has given India a historic Asian Games medal.
Article Summary: Jay Meena was bedridden with typhoid and a severe infection, losing eight kilograms in the process. The 25-year-old needed his parents to feed him by hand for nearly a week. He recovered just in time to board the flight to Tokyo and the Shinkansen (train) to Nagoya.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: Gulveer Singh headlines India's athletics surge
Article Text:
India's Gulveer Singh. (PTI Photo/Arun Sharma)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Moments after finishing his 10,000m race, Gulveer Singh went down on his knees. He touched the ground, then fell on his back and briefly looked up at the sky. When he got up he flashed a smile, which was probably brighter than the silver he had just won. From the bronze from Hangzhou, the upgrade was deserving. The medal was probably loading since June 28, when he won India’s maiden 10,000m at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.At the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Friday night, Gulveer came home in 28:29.38 minutes to finish between two African-born Bahrain citizens. While Birhanu Balew clinched gold with a time of 28:27.51 minutes, Albert Kipto ended third in 28:34.18.Gulveer, the 28-year-old from Atrauli was tactically sharp and focused on not falling behind. By the fifth lap, he was third in a leader pack of six athletes. He rarely fell behind, barring the midrace when he briefly occupied the fifth position. With four laps to go, the Naib Subedar in the Army upped the pace and moved to second position. By that time the front runners had left behind the rest of the field, with the sixth-placed runner almost 150m behind.When the bell to signal the last lap was rang, it felt like it kicked an adrenaline rush in the eventual podium finishers, with the final 200m more like a sprint race with Balew in top gear. An elated Gulveer later said, “It feels good to win a silver for India at the Asian Games. It is very satisfying.”Gulveer, who like most of the other distance runners trains in Colorado Springs, said, “Races such as these are different from races where you’re chasing time. I trusted the race plan of the coaches, which was to stay relaxed, remain with the lead group, and make my move at the right moment.”Baranica Elangovan suffered a career threatening injury in 2019 and it took her a couple years to find her way back. She raised the bar gradually, until she became the first woman pole vaulter to clinch a medal at the competition. A late bloomer who switched from long jump and triple jump on the insistence of her coach Milber Bertrand Russell, cleared 4.15 metres on her fifth attempt to take the bronze, while the gold stayed at home with Misaki Morota’s personal best of 4.55, earning her the top spot. Chunge Niu (4.50m) of China was secondOn a milestone medal, the 29-year-old said, “It’s always been my dream to rewrite history and I’ve done that today. That said, I’m really happy that I could win a medal for the country.” Such was Baranica’s focus that she didn’t realise she had won a medal until her compatriot Sindhushree Ganesh, who ended last with no mark, told her.“When Sindhu told me, I didn’t believe her. I checked, re-checked and checked again. Only then did I believe the medal was mine. When I saw the medal icon against my name, I signalled to my coach Russell in the stands to check again,” said the athlete, who hails from a farmer’s family in Kuthalam in Tamil Nadu.From the ignominy of a four-year dope ban to standing on the podium at the continental event, Manpreet Kaur’s life has come full circle. Watched by her teenage daughter, the shot putter with a fourth attempt throw of 17.17 metres won bronze behind the Chinese duo of Song Jiayuan (19.40m) and Zhang Linru (18.14m), who won gold and silver, respectively. Manpreet, who returned from the ban in 2021, was slow off the mark with a 16.32, while he best came in her penultimate attempt. The other Indian in the fray, Krishna Jayasankar Menon, finished fifth with a best effort of 16.57m.
Article Summary: Gulveer came home in 28:29.38 minutes to finish between two African-born Bahrain citizens. Birhanu Balew clinched gold with a time of 28:27.51 minutes, Albert Kipto ended third in28:34.18.

Article Title: Anshul Kamboj exploits tricky Puducherry pitch as India ‘A’ beat Australia ‘A’
Article Text:
Anshul Kamboj (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brief scores:

PUDUCHERRY: The heat in Puducherry was unforgiving. The pitch offered little movement for the pace bowlers. Yet, India ‘A’ paceman Anshul Kamboj found a way to make things work.Kamboj was the first to strike in the morning session, using the cracks and variable bounce to dismiss Australia ‘A’ batters Nathan McSweeney and Peter Handscomb in consecutive overs to set up a 162-run win in the first unofficial Test here on Friday. McSweeney was surprised by the extra bounce before Handscomb was beaten by one that stayed low and crashed into the off stump.Left-arm spinner Shams Mulani (3-57) and medium-pacer Tushar Deshpande (3-14) took three wickets apiece as the Aussies folded for 200 while chasing 363 in the last innings.Kamboj, after returning figures of 2-25, said that the conditions were difficult for the pacers. “It was too hot for fast bowling. You have to put in a lot of effort to maintain the intensity. I am very happy that I am able to maintain that,” Kamboj said after the win.The surface, with its “whitish soil” and limited bounce, demanded discipline and an understanding of the areas to bowl in. “This is whitish soil. So here it was just that we always have to keep the wickets in play and bowl within stumps,” he said.Kamboj first underlined his red-ball credentials with an eight-wicket innings haul in Duleep Trophy and then produced a 10-wicket innings haul against Kerala in Ranji Trophy in 2024.His reward came in July 2025 when he was handed his Test debut at Old Trafford. He took 1-89 before being left out after that.Kamboj, though, refuses to see one match as a setback. “I am not trying to change anything. If one or two matches go wrong in your career, it doesn’t mean that you are bad. Everyone can see your hard work. If I just keep working hard, the results will fall in favour,” the 25-year-old said.He was also CSK’s leading wicket-taker in the 2026 season, finishing with 21 scalps. Now he has another opportunity to take his game to another level under new head coach Zaheer Khan. “I am very excited to meet him. I had a camp with him in CoE in Bengaluru.”India ‘A’ 334 & 199. Australia ‘A’ 171 & 200 (F O'Neill 47; T Deshpande 3-14, S Mulani 3-57). India ‘A’ won by 162 runs.Pandya suffers fresh shin injury, out of NZ series: Hardik Pandya has suffered a fresh right-shin injury and is set to miss at least three weeks, ruling him out of India’s white-ball tour of New Zealand. He was earler picked for India A’s One Day series against Australia ‘A’.
Article Summary: Anshul Kamboj takes 2-25 as India 'A' win first unofficial Test in Puducherry. Shams Mulani and Tushar Deshpande take three wickets each as Aussies folded for 200. Hardik Pandya ruled out of white-ball tour of New Zealand with shin injury.

Article Title: India women storm into Asian Games hockey semifinals with 3-1 win over Japan
Article Text:
Indian women's hockey team

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NAGOYA: With 59 goals from four matches and another to go, the Indian women’s hockey team stormed into the semifinals on Friday after easing past hosts Japan 3-1 at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium.Playing an attacking brand of hockey, India took the lead through Lalremsiami in the fifth minute. Japan threatened on the counter and enjoyed periods of possession, but India remained in control of the game.Ishika doubled India’s lead in the 30th minute, scoring from the rebound after Japanese goalkeeper Yu Kudo saved Navneet Kaur’s penalty-corner attempt.India extended their advantage six minutes later when Navneet scooped the ball over the goalkeeper’s head to make it 3-0.Japan managed to pull one back through Shiho Kobayakawa in the 46th minute, but India held their nerve in the closing stages to prevent the hosts from making a comeback.After scoring goals by the dozen in their earlier matches, India faced their first real test of the competition. Japan’s speed and agility helped them control possession, with the hosts enjoying 58% of the ball.However, the biggest difference between the two teams was their execution.Japan earned six penalty corners, particularly through their counter-attacking play, but failed to convert any of them. They also did well defensively, restricting India to just two penalty corners.India’s chief coach Sjoerd Marijne admitted his team could have scored more goals and needed to cut down on mistakes.“We played well but we needed to score more goals. Also, we gave away possession easily a few times. Silly mistakes have to go out of our play,” he told TOI.India will play Singapore in their final match on Saturday, but Marijne is already focused on the knockout stage and believes his side needs to raise its intensity.“Ahead of the semis, it was important to bring that energy back into our game,” he said.
Article Summary: India beat hosts Japan 3-1 to reach semifinals of women's World Cup. India have now scored 59 goals from four matches. India will play Singapore in their final match on Saturday. India's chief coach Sjoerd Marijne admitted his team could have scored more goals.

Earlier, Gulveer Singh won silver in the men's 10,000m, while Naorem Roshibina Devi took silver in women's sanda 60kg and Mirabai Chanu ended her long wait for an Asian Games medal with silver in the women's 49kg weightlifting event.India's latest bronze came from Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar, who lost their mixed doubles semifinal against Hong Kong's Lee Ka Yi and Tang Ming Hong in a thrilling 1-2 contest.The Indian pair fought back after losing the opening game 10-11 to dominate the second 11-2. Carlos Rodon’s latest philanthropic honor is very much tied to one of the most personal chapters of his life outside of baseball. The New York Yankees pitcher and his wife, Ashley Rodon, suffered two miscarriages before welcoming their daughter Willow and raising a family of three children. That experience became the launching pad for a nonprofit that helps other families who are experiencing infertility and pregnancy loss.The Players Trust announced Rodon as the season’s final Most Valuable Philanthropist honoree on September 23, 2026. In addition to the recognition, The Players Trust also presented a $10,000 grant to the Carlos Rodon Foundation, which will offer the organization additional funding to help families dealing with financial struggles connected to fertility issues.The Players Trust named Carlos Rodon its Most Valuable Philanthropist for September, an award that honors MLB players for their charitable work and impact on their community outside of the game of baseball. The September award is the last of its kind for the 2026 season and comes with a $10,000 grant to the charity of the recipient’s choice.Rodon’s money will be directed to the Carlos Rodon Foundation, the nonprofit he and his wife Ashley Rodon created.The organization seeks to help couples and families struggling with infertility and pregnancy loss, especially by reducing some of the financial barriers associated with fertility treatment.Rodon’s dedication to the cause is linked to his own family’s experience, the Players Trust said. Chris Capuano, chairman of the Players Trust Board of Trustees, noted Rodon’s decision to share that experience while helping those in similar situations.The Carlos Rodon Foundation was established in 2024 after Carlos and Ashley Rodon experienced two miscarriages as they tried to start their family. The foundation said their experience, which led them to undergo fertility treatment, led them to decide to set up an organization to help other families facing similar financial and emotional challenges.Its flagship program is the Willow Grant, named after the Rodons’ daughter, Willow. The program is designed to assist eligible families with infertility following pregnancy loss who are seeking fertility treatment, including IVF. The foundation says its bigger mission is to help families find treatment and resources while lowering the financial burden that comes with growing a family.That work has become much larger in scale. By September 2026, the foundation had granted $715,000 to 60 families in 17 states. The organization also reported 34 families were currently in treatment, with 15 babies on the way and four babies born through Willow Grant support.Fundraising efforts have also been stepped up alongside the foundation’s grant program. Its annual Willow Gala has become a major source of support. By September 2026, the New York Yankees reported the event had raised more than $1.8 million in three years. The foundation’s progress, as reported by NC State Athletics, said more than $1 million was raised by the August 2026 gala alone.The organization has also formed partnerships that are focused on treating treatment-related expenses. An example is its partnership with Alto Pharmacy to help lower the cost of fertility medications for grant recipients. In addition to direct financial support through the Willow Grant, these efforts are.Carlos Rodon's charitable work has evolved with his MLB career. The lefty debuted in the big leagues with the Chicago White Sox in 2015 and spent time with the San Francisco Giants before joining the New York Yankees after the 2022 season. A three-time All-Star, he pitched a no-hitter for Chicago in 2021.But the mission of the foundation springs from a chapter of his life that precedes much of its current scope. Ashley Rodon has spoken about the couple’s two miscarriages and the uncertainty that has come with their attempts to have children. Eventually, their daughter, Willow, was born, and soon the couple had three children, and her name became part of the central grant program of the foundation.Ashley Rodon has been an active leader in the organization as its executive director and co-founder. Her work, according to the foundation, is focused on offering support to families, raising awareness about infertility and pregnancy loss, and helping to ease the loneliness that comes with those experiences.Therefore, the $10,000 Players Trust grant becomes another addition to an already greatly expanded effort. The award is not a separate program, but additional resources for an existing foundation that works to provide fertility assistance and pregnancy-loss support.Rodon’s September honor follows a broader streak of recognition for his community work. He was named the Yankees’ nominee for the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award, and the Players Trust award directs $10,000 toward that same foundation. All told, the developments have shone a light on a charitable cause that dates back to the Rodon family’s own experience.The newest grant is just another avenue of funding for families facing the financial burdens of infertility and pregnancy loss for the Carlos Rodon Foundation. Its purported reach in 17 states shows how the organization has expanded beyond the story of the Rodon family itself into a broader network of support for those seeking fertility treatment.

That experience became the launching pad for a nonprofit that helps other families who are experiencing infertility and pregnancy loss. By September 2026, the foundation had granted $715,000 to 60 families.

He completed 17 of 33 passes for 164 yards and two touchdowns in Texas’ 30 6 win. The Houston Chronicle reported that the Longhorns’ offense struggled for much of the game.Steve Sarkisian has also pointed to an issue that could become important in Knoxville. After the UTSA game, the Texas coach said Manning may have relied too much on his legs instead of staying patient through his reads.“I thought Arch kind of fell in love with his legs a little bit tonight. His legs are a really good weapon,” Sarkisian said. “But what happens when you go to run? You can start speeding up through your progressions, and I think that’s why we don’t want to make a living with him running the ball as much as he ran tonight.”Tennessee’s defense can also make Texas work for every possession. The Volunteers had recorded 11 sacks and 20 tackles for loss through two games, according to Tennessee Athletics.Manning enters with 60 completions on 97 attempts for 664 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. The question is how often Texas can give him the ball if Tennessee controls the clock.The game carries a family angle. Manning visits Neyland for the first time, where uncle Peyton Manning starred. Texas and Tennessee have not played since 1969 and now meet as SEC opponents, according to AP.For Arch Manning, the task is clear Saturday. Make the most of his chances, stay patient and avoid giving Tennessee easy opportunities. If the Volunteers keep running the ball, those chances may be limited.

Article Title: Nick Bosa is ruled out again as his comeback lasts just two games, Cardinals curse continues
Article Text:

Nick Bosa's long-awaited return to the San Francisco 49ers has hit another frustrating roadblock. The star defensive end suffered a calf injury during Thursday's practice and is expected to miss a few weeks, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. Bosa will miss Sunday's Week 3 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, with the 49ers still determining whether he will be placed on injured reserve. The latest setback comes just two games into Bosa's return from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season after only three appearances.Bosa entered the 2026 season after spending much of the previous year working his way back from the second ACL injury of his NFL career. The 49ers had been cautious with his workload throughout the offseason. San Francisco general manager John Lynch said before training camp that Bosa had been cleared to begin working his way back, while emphasizing that the team would gradually increase his workload during his recovery.That patience appeared to pay off when Bosa was available for the season opener against the Los Angeles Rams. He then played again in Week 2 against the Miami Dolphins. According to the 49ers' official player log, Bosa recorded four tackles and three tackles for loss in Week 1 before adding three tackles against Miami in Week 2.Now, instead of building momentum after his comeback, Bosa is facing another spell on the sidelines.The calf issue surfaced only days before the 49ers were scheduled to face the Cardinals, the same team Bosa was playing against when he suffered his ACL injury last season.Bosa was initially listed as dealing with soreness during training camp and had been managed carefully as he returned from the ACL injury. This time, however, the injury is expected to keep him out for multiple weeks.The 49ers are reportedly considering injured reserve, although the team is leaning against that option at this stage. If Bosa is placed on IR, he would be required to miss at least four games.Bosa's absence is also significant because San Francisco is already dealing with injuries along its defensive front. The team has had several defensive linemen miss time, adding pressure on the remaining players to fill Bosa's role while he recovers. The 49ers' official injury report has also listed defensive linemen including Romello Height and James Thompson Jr. among players missing practice this week.For a defense built around Bosa's ability to generate pressure off the edge, replacing his production will be a major challenge. The five-time Pro Bowler remains one of the centerpiece players on San Francisco's defense, making even a short-term absence particularly significant.There is no indication at this point that the calf injury is connected to another ACL problem, and the current reporting points to an absence of, rather than a season-ending injury.That distinction is important given what Bosa has already gone through. He missed almost the entirety of the 2025 season after tearing his ACL in Week 3 and spent the offseason working toward his return. The 49ers had finally gotten their defensive star back on the field, only for another injury to interrupt his comeback after two games.For now, San Francisco will have to move forward without its premier pass rusher while Bosa focuses on getting back to full health.
Article Summary: Nick Bosa suffered a calf injury during Thursday's practice and is expected to miss a few weeks, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. Bosa will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals, with the 49ers still determining whether he will be placed on injured reserve. The latest setback comes just two games into Bosa's return from the torn ACL that ended his 2025 season after only three appearances.

India beat Iran 37-33 to clinch the gold medal in the women's kabaddi event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Saturday, adding another gold to the country's medal tally.The victory marks India's fourth gold medal in women's kabaddi at the Asian Games. The Indian team had previously won gold in 2010, 2014 and 2022, while finishing runners-up in 2018.India entered the final as defending champions after beating Chinese Taipei 26-25 in the gold-medal match at the Hangzhou Games.The gold also adds to a productive morning for India on September 26. Before the kabaddi final, Sawan Barwal won silver in the men's marathon, while Ashi Chouksey, Tilottama Sen and Vidarsa Vinod claimed silver in the women's 50m rifle 3 positions team event. Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar also secured bronze in squash mixed doubles.Barwal clocked 2:11:37 to end India's 44-year wait for a men's marathon medal at the Asian Games. It was India's first medal in the event since the 1982 Delhi Games.In shooting, India's trio of Ashi, Tilottama and Vidarsa finished second in the women's 50m rifle 3 positions team event. Tilottama and Vidarsa also progressed to the individual final, while Ashi missed out after finishing 15th in qualification.Joshna and Velavan secured the squash mixed doubles bronze after reaching the semifinals. They had defeated the Philippines' David Pelino and Jemyca Aribado 11-3, 11-5 in the quarterfinals before losing a close semifinal to Hong Kong's Lee Ka Yi and Tang Ming Hong.India had entered Saturday with 26 medals — two gold, 11 silver and 13 bronze — and stood 12th in the standings. The women's kabaddi gold takes India's tally to 27 medals: three gold, 11 silver and 13 bronze.India's men's kabaddi team will also chase gold later on Saturday, facing Iran in the men's final. Both Indian teams had entered the Games as defending champions.

Article Title: 'You will be handed a few wins': Amid SIR row, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke asks opposition parties to stop contesting in 'rigged' polls
Article Text:

‘Cannot talk about rigging selectively’

(With inputs from PTI)
