NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has urged opposition parties to stop participating in elections if they believe the electoral process is being rigged, arguing that continued participation gives legitimacy to polls they themselves question.In a post on X on Friday, Dipke said opposition parties could not claim that elections were being rigged while continuing to contest them."Yes, elections are being rigged. But when you continue to participate in rigged elections, you legitimise these elections and help maintain the illusion that they are free and fair," he said.Dipke questioned whether opposition parties continued to contest elections because they feared losing their political presence if they stayed away."Maybe you keep contesting because you fear that if you don't, you will stop existing. But what kind of existence are you trying to protect when votes are being stolen, your MLAs and MPs are being poached, and your parties are being split?" he said."This is not political survival. You are simply trying to stay alive in a system that can weaken you, split your party or take away your elected representatives whenever it wants.How long can you survive like this?" Dipke asked.The CJP founder also accused opposition parties of raising allegations of election rigging selectively, depending on the state or political party involved."And you cannot talk about election rigging only when it happens in states that matter to you and remain silent when it happens elsewhere. If elections are being rigged, it should matter regardless of the state or which party is affected," the CJP convener said."You cannot keep saying the game is rigged while continuing to play it. Your participation is the only thing that gives these rigged elections legitimacy," he claimed.Dipke appealed to opposition parties to put democracy ahead of their political interests."Think about the nation and its democracy before thinking about your own political survival. Take a stand and stop participating in rigged elections."Dipke compared an allegedly manipulated election to a fixed cricket match, saying an election could still appear competitive even if its outcome had been predetermined."Just like in a fixed match, not every catch is dropped. Some catches are taken, and the match may even be dragged to the last over to make it look like a close fight," he said."In the same way, you will be handed a few wins, just enough to keep you contesting and to make people believe there was a real contest. Those few wins are the crumbs that keep you in the game and make the whole thing look legitimate," Dipke said.The remarks came a day after Dipke demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and threatened to launch a "Jantar Mantar 2.0" agitation if his demand was not met.They also followed a report by The Indian Express on Wednesday that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the previous 10 months to decisions and orders of the Election Commission, including those concerning the addition, deletion and restoration of voters and changes to the voter registration process.Following the report, poll panel officials said the two commissioners had flagged decisions taken during voter-roll cleanup and the handling of the voter database in various states.EC sources maintained that all decisions of the Election Commission of India , including SIR, had been unanimous and approved by both election commissioners and the chief election commissioner.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has urged opposition parties to stop participating in elections if they believe the electoral process is being rigged. He said opposition parties could not claim that elections were being rigged while continuing to contest them. Dipke compared an allegedly manipulated election to a fixed cricket match.

Article Title: 30 rescued after fire breaks out in multi-storey building housing Haldiram’s outlet in Delhi’s Model Town
Article Text:
A fire broke out in a three-storey building housing a Haldiram's outlet in northwest Delhi's Model Town area





DELHI: Around 30 people were rescued after a fire broke out in a three-storey building housing a Haldiram outlet and adjoining structures in northwest Delhi's Model Town area on Friday, officials said.The fire broke out around 2pm, following which head constable Pawan, the beat officer of Model Town police station, became the first responder and alerted senior officers, news agency PTI reported.Thick smoke was seen billowing from the building, which has a basement, ground floor and three upper floors.The Delhi fire service received a call about the blaze at around 2.40pm and initially rushed four fire tenders to the spot.As the fire intensified, the DFS deployed 23 units, including a hydraulic platform, officials said.The police team evacuated occupants of the affected building as well as those in adjoining buildings, safely rescuing a total of 30 people, police said."The building has a basement, ground and three floors. On the ground and first floor there is Haldiram and on the second and third floor there is one more restaurant.The fire was on all the floors. We have searched the entire building and no one was trapped inside," a DFS officer said.The blaze, suspected to have been caused by a short circuit, broke out in a multi-storey building housing the Haldiram outlet and other establishments, PTI reported."The fire was classified as a medium fire at 3.30pm and was brought under control around 4pm," he said.Md Sajid, assistant bank manager of a private bank, said, "As soon as the short circuit happened, the guard informed us that a fire had broken out and we should evacuate the building. The fire started on the ground floor and engulfed the whole building. We used a fire extinguisher in our office to try to extinguish the fire as much as we could on an individual level."No injury or casualty was reported due to the timely police response and prompt evacuation, officials said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: A fire broke out in a three-storey building housing a Haldiram outlet in northwest Delhi's Model Town area on Friday. The Delhi fire service received a call about the blaze at around 2.40pm and initially rushed four fire tenders to the spot. As the fire intensified, the DFS deployed 23 units, including a hydraulic platform, officials said.

Article Title: Baranica Elangovan scripts history, wins India's first-ever pole vault medal at Asian Games
Article Text:
Baranica Elangovan in action during the Women's Pole Vault Final

Indian athlete Baranica Elangovan won the bronze medal in the women's pole vault at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Friday, giving India its first-ever medal in the event at the Asian Games.The 29-year-old secured the bronze with a best clearance of 4.15m. She shared the medal with Kazakhstan's Polina Ivanova, who also cleared 4.15m. The two athletes matched each other on countback, resulting in a shared bronze.Baranica began with first-attempt clearances of 3.85m and 4.00m before needing two attempts to clear 4.15m. She then attempted 4.25m but failed on all three attempts, ending her competition with the bronze medal.Her compatriot Sindhushree Ganesha exited the competition without registering a mark, while Baranica remained in contention for a medal.Baranica has also had a strong season, improving the national record twice earlier this year. She first cleared 4.22m in March and then raised the mark to 4.23m in May at Bhubaneswar. Sindhushree G later improved the national record to 4.25m in June. Baranica's season-best remains 4.23m.The pole vaulter from Tamil Nadu had suffered an ACL injury in 2020 and went through a challenging period of rehabilitation, after which she moved to the Reliance Foundation High Performance Centre in Bhubaneswar in 2023.Japan's Misaki Morota won the gold with a best clearance of 4.55m, while China's Chunge Neu took silver with 4.50m.Baranica's bronze took India's overall medal tally at the Asian Games to 23, including two gold, nine silver and 12 bronze medals.
